name: Bow Rake with 54 in Wood Handle
title: Bow Rake with 54 in Wood Handle for Cleanup
h1: Bow Rake with 54 in Wood Handle
meta: A steel bow rake with a 54 in wood handle for jobsite cleanup: pulling chips, leveling mulch, and raking sawdust and twigs off lawns after tree work.
tagline: A stiff steel-head rake for chip cleanup, mulch, and finish raking on tree jobs.
summary: This bow rake pairs a rigid steel head with a 54 in wood handle, the size most ground crews reach for when the brush is chipped and the yard still needs to look clean. It moves chips, sawdust, and small debris without flexing like a leaf rake.
highlights: Pulls chips, sawdust, and small debris
Flat back for leveling mulch and soil

body.h: Where a bow rake earns its spot on the truck
p: Cleanup is the part of the job the customer remembers. After the chipper is done, there is always a layer of chips, sawdust, and snapped twigs under the drop zone and along the path to the truck. A leaf rake skates over that material. A bow rake digs into it and pulls it into a pile you can shovel or blow onto a tarp.

Flip the head over and the flat back works for spreading mulch, smoothing a stump-grinding hole after backfill, or knocking down ruts left by a loader. The 54 in handle gives enough reach to work without bending all day.

Keep the rake out of the chipper infeed zone and never use it to push brush toward the rollers; feed with branches, not hand tools. Store it head-down or hung so the handle does not warp, and sand and oil the wood once a season if it starts to splinter.
Steel tines can bend if you pry roots or rocks with them. Use a mattock or bar for that and save the rake for raking. More cleanup tools are in our landscaper tools section.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bow rake and a leaf rake?
faq.a: A bow rake has short, rigid steel tines for moving heavy material like chips, soil, and gravel. A leaf rake has long, flexible tines meant for light leaves and grass.

faq.q: Is a 54 in handle long enough?
faq.a: For most adults it is a comfortable working length that lets you stand fairly upright while raking chips and mulch.

name: Hasegawa Orchard Ladder, Platform Style
title: Hasegawa Orchard Ladder, Platform Style: Guide
meta: The Hasegawa orchard ladder in platform style is a three-leg aluminum tripod ladder with a standing platform for pruning hedges, orchards, and small trees.
tagline: A tripod orchard ladder with a flat platform top for steady pruning work.
summary: The Hasegawa orchard ladder, platform style, is a three-legged aluminum tripod ladder topped with a small standing platform instead of a narrow top rung. It gives pruners and hedge crews a steadier place to stand on soft or uneven ground than a step ladder.
highlights: Three-leg tripod design for uneven ground
Platform top for a steadier stance
Adjustable third leg on most models
Common in orchards, Japanese gardens, and hedge work

body.h: Why tripod ladders work in the landscape
p: A four-legged step ladder needs flat, firm ground. Lawns, beds, and slopes rarely give you that. A tripod ladder puts two legs on the rungs side and a single pole leg out back, so it settles into soft soil and can be set with the back leg up a slope or tucked into a hedge. Hasegawa is a Japanese maker known for these ladders in orchards and garden pruning.

The platform-style top gives you a flat place to plant both feet, which helps when you are working shears or a hand saw overhead for a long stretch. It is a pruning ladder for hedges, fruit trees, and ornamental work, not a substitute for climbing or an aerial lift on bigger trees.

Set the ladder on ground that will not wash out under a leg, push the back leg in firmly, and keep your body centered between the rails. Do not stand above the level the manufacturer marks, and never lean out past your hips. Check the ladder's duty rating and follow Hasegawa's instructions, along with the ladder requirements in ANSI Z133.

Inspect the feet, rivets, and hinge before each use and retire a ladder with bent rails. Platform heights vary by model, so pick one that lets you reach the work without stretching. Browse more landscaper tools.

faq.q: Is a tripod orchard ladder stable?
faq.a: Set correctly on soft ground with the back leg pushed in, a tripod ladder is very steady. On hard, slick surfaces it can slip, so it suits lawns, beds, and orchards best.

faq.q: What height should I buy?
faq.a: Choose the shortest model that lets you reach the work from a standing position at or below the highest step the manufacturer allows.

name: Husqvarna Logger Tape, 50 ft (15 m)
title: Husqvarna Logger Tape 50 ft (15 m) for Bucking
meta: The Husqvarna logger tape is a 50 ft (15 m) belt-mounted measuring tape with a nail hook for marking bucking lengths on logs, firewood, and saw logs.
tagline: A belt-worn, self-retracting tape for measuring log lengths solo.
summary: The Husqvarna logger tape is a 50 ft (15 m) self-retracting measuring tape that clips to your belt so you can measure and mark log lengths without a helper. Hook the nail into the end of the log, walk out, and mark your cut.
highlights: Nail hook end grips the log
Useful for saw logs, firewood, and slab lengths

p: When a customer wants the trunk left in 16 in rounds for firewood, or a mill wants saw logs at set lengths, guessing with the bar wastes wood. A logger tape lets one person hook the end of the log, walk the length, and scribe a mark with the saw at each cut point. The tape retracts as you walk back, so it stays out of the chips.
A 50 ft tape covers most saw log lengths with room for trim allowance. It also works for laying out a drop zone or checking the distance to a structure before felling.

Retract the tape and keep it clear before you start cutting; a tape blade near a running chain gets cut fast. Wear your chaps and keep good footing when walking a log, especially on slopes or wet bark.
The nail and blade are wear items. Replacement nails and refills are available for many logger tapes, so a damaged blade does not mean buying the whole unit. See more forestry tools.

faq.q: How do you use a logger tape alone?
faq.a: Clip the case to your belt, set the nail hook into the end of the log, walk to the length you need, and mark the log. The spring pulls the tape back as you return.

faq.q: Can I replace the tape blade?
faq.a: Many logger tapes accept refill blades and replacement nails. Check that the refill matches the case model before ordering.

name: Spencer 75 ft Diameter Tape Refill
title: Spencer 75 ft Diameter Tape Refill Blade
meta: A Spencer diameter tape refill restores a worn 75 ft logging tape so you can keep measuring tree diameter and log lengths without buying a new case.
tagline: A replacement 75 ft blade for a Spencer diameter tape case.
summary: This Spencer diameter tape refill is a replacement 75 ft blade for a Spencer tape case. Diameter tapes read tree diameter directly when wrapped around a trunk, which makes them a standard tool for foresters, consulting arborists, and tree inventory work.
highlights: Replacement 75 ft blade for a Spencer case
Diameter scale for reading DBH directly
Keeps a good case in service
Faster than buying a complete tape

p: Diameter at breast height (DBH) drives a lot of decisions: tree inventories, appraisals, removal quotes, protection ordinances, and dosing for plant health treatments. A diameter tape is graduated so that when you wrap it around the trunk, the reading is the diameter, not the circumference. No math, no rounding errors in the field.
Blades take a beating. They get kinked on bark, cut on brush, and worn where they rub the case. A refill lets you swap just the blade and keep the case you already trust.

Match the refill to your Spencer case model and length before you order; refills are made for specific cases. Follow Spencer's instructions to remove the old blade and wind in the new one, and keep the case free of grit so the new blade retracts smoothly.
Wrap the tape level and snug around the trunk at the height your standard calls for, usually 4.5 ft above grade in the US. More measuring tools are in forestry tools.

faq.q: What is a diameter tape?
faq.a: A tape graduated in units of diameter (circumference divided by pi), so wrapping it around a trunk gives the tree's diameter directly.

faq.q: Will this refill fit any tape case?
faq.a: No. Refills are made for specific Spencer case models and lengths, so confirm your case before ordering.

name: Spencer Logging Tape Measure, 50 ft with Nail (Model 950)
title: Spencer Logging Tape 50 ft with Nail, Model 950
h1: Spencer Logging Tape Measure, 50 ft, Model 950
meta: The Spencer logging tape, Model 950, is a 50 ft belt-worn tape with a nail end for measuring and marking log lengths solo. Uses, care, and refills explained.
tagline: A 50 ft belt-clip logging tape with a nail end for one-person bucking.
summary: The Spencer logging tape Model 950 is a 50 ft self-retracting tape with a nail end, built to clip on your belt so one person can measure log lengths on the landing or in the woods. Spencer tapes have long been a fixture with loggers and timber crews.
highlights: Built for loggers and tree crews

p: Set the nail into the end grain, walk the log, and mark each cut with a nick from the saw or a lumber crayon. The tape pulls back as you return, so it does not drag through mud and chips. That is the whole point of a logging tape: fast, accurate lengths with nobody holding the dumb end.
For tree crews it is handy whenever the wood is going somewhere specific: a sawmill, a woodworker, or firewood customers who want a set round length.

Retract the blade before you cut and keep it away from the chain. Wipe sap and grit off the blade so it does not wear the case or jam on return. When the nail wears or breaks, replace it rather than retiring the tape, and swap in a refill blade when the markings wear off or the blade kinks.
Wear chaps and keep good footing when walking logs. Find nails, refills, and more in forestry tools.

faq.q: Does the Spencer 950 use a replaceable nail?
faq.a: Yes. Replacement nails are sold separately, so a worn or broken nail is an easy fix.

faq.q: Is 50 ft long enough?
faq.a: It covers common saw log and firewood lengths. Longer tapes are available if you regularly measure long logs or pole lengths.

name: Spencer Logging Tape Replacement Nail
title: Spencer Logging Tape Replacement Nail
meta: A Spencer logging tape replacement nail puts a worn or broken tape back to work. It hooks into end grain so you can measure log lengths without a helper.
tagline: A replacement end nail that keeps your Spencer logging tape in service.
summary: The Spencer logging tape replacement nail fixes the part of a logging tape that wears out first: the hooked nail at the end of the blade. A fresh nail bites into end grain and holds while you walk the log, so you get accurate lengths again.
highlights: Replaces a worn, bent, or broken tape nail
Restores solid grip in end grain
Cheaper than a new tape or refill
Small enough to keep spares in the truck
Confirm fit with your tape model

p: A logging tape only works if the end stays put while you walk out the length. A dull, bent, or missing nail pulls out of the end grain halfway down the log, and you lose the measurement. That makes the nail the most common replacement part on the tape, and it is worth keeping a couple in the truck.
Swapping the nail is quicker and cheaper than replacing the blade or the whole tape, and it keeps a tape you know is accurate in service.

Follow Spencer's instructions for your tape model. Make sure the new nail is seated firmly on the blade end and that the tape still reads correctly against a known length after the swap. A loose nail can throw off every cut.
Retract the tape and keep it clear of the chain before you start cutting. More tapes, refills, and parts are in forestry tools.

faq.q: How do I know if I need a new nail?
faq.a: If the nail slips out of end grain, is bent, or is visibly worn down, replace it.

faq.q: Does it fit every Spencer tape?
faq.a: Spencer tapes vary by model, so confirm the nail matches your tape before ordering.

name: LogRite Log Stand Attachment
title: LogRite Log Stand Attachment for Cant Hooks
meta: The LogRite log stand attachment lifts a log off the ground so you can buck it without running the chain into dirt. How it works with LogRite tools.
tagline: An add-on stand that turns a LogRite tool into a log lifter for clean bucking.
summary: The LogRite log stand attachment adds a foot to a LogRite cant hook or peavey so you can roll a log up and hold it off the ground while you buck. Keeping the cut clear of soil saves your chain and speeds up firewood and cleanup work.
highlights: Converts a LogRite tool into a log lifter
Holds the log up off the dirt
Saves chain from rocks and soil
Pairs with LogRite cant hooks and peaveys
specs: LogRite cant hooks and peaveys (check model)

p: Bucking a log that is lying on the ground means the last inch of every cut runs toward dirt and stones. One touch and the chain is dull. Rolling the log up onto a stand gets the cut zone off the ground so you can saw straight through. It also brings the work up a few inches, which your back will notice by the end of a removal.
LogRite tools are known for their aluminum handles and hooks built for hard use. The stand attachment lets one tool do double duty: roll and position the log, then lift and hold it.

Make sure the log is stable on the stand before you cut, and stand to the uphill side. Watch for pinching as the cut opens and keep your feet clear of where the log will drop. Wear chaps, boots, eye and hearing protection.
Check fit against your LogRite model and handle size before ordering, and follow LogRite's instructions for mounting. More tools are in log handling tools.

faq.q: Does it fit any cant hook?
faq.a: It is made for LogRite tools. Confirm the fit with your specific LogRite model before ordering.

faq.q: What size logs can it lift?
faq.a: Capacity depends on the tool and log. Follow LogRite's guidance and do not overload the handle.

name: Husqvarna 540iXP Rear-Handle Battery Chainsaw Kit
title: Husqvarna 540iXP Battery Chainsaw Kit: Buying Guide
meta: The Husqvarna 540iXP is a pro rear-handle battery chainsaw on the 36V platform. See what the kit is for, how it runs on tree jobs, and battery choices.
tagline: A professional rear-handle battery saw for ground work, limbing, and quiet jobs.
summary: The Husqvarna 540iXP is a professional rear-handle battery chainsaw on Husqvarna's 36V platform, sold here as a kit with battery and charger. It suits ground crews for limbing, bucking small wood, and jobs where noise and fumes matter.
highlights: Quiet, no fuel mixing, instant start
Kit format for getting started on battery
Shares batteries with other Husqvarna 36V tools

p: Battery saws have earned a place on tree crews for ground work. The 540iXP starts with a trigger pull, runs quiet enough for early starts in neighborhoods, and does not need mixed fuel. It handles limbing brush for the chipper, bucking small wood, and cleanup cuts well. For large-diameter felling and bucking, a gas saw is still the tool.
Being a rear-handle saw, it is meant for use on the ground. Climbers working aloft use top-handle models like the T540iXP, which are designed for that job.

Runtime depends on the battery and the wood. A bigger pack such as the BLi200X or BLi300 gives longer runs, and many crews carry spares in the truck. Keep packs out of direct sun and charge them per Husqvarna's instructions.

Check chain tension and bar oil often; battery saws are quiet enough that a dull chain is easy to miss. Wear chaps, eye, ear, and head protection, and get trained before running any chainsaw. More battery tools are in battery-powered equipment.

faq.q: Can I climb with the 540iXP?
faq.a: It is a rear-handle saw intended for ground use. Use a top-handle saw designed for in-tree work when climbing, and only if trained to do so.

faq.q: Which batteries does it use?
faq.a: It runs on Husqvarna's 36V battery line, such as the BLi200X and BLi300.

name: Husqvarna BLi200X Battery
title: Husqvarna BLi200X 36V Battery: Specs and Uses
meta: The Husqvarna BLi200X is a 36V Li-ion battery for pro battery saws, blowers, and trimmers. Capacity, what it runs, and how to get long life from it.
tagline: A 36V pro battery pack for Husqvarna saws, blowers, and trimmers.
summary: The Husqvarna BLi200X is a 36V lithium-ion battery that powers Husqvarna's professional battery saws, blowers, and trimmers. It clips straight into the tool, which makes it a common pick for climbers running a T540iXP aloft.
highlights: Light enough to run in a top-handle saw
Charge level indicator on the pack

p: On a battery top-handle saw, the battery is part of the weight you carry up the tree. The BLi200X sits in the sweet spot: enough capacity for a good stretch of pruning cuts, without the bulk of the larger packs. On the ground it runs rear-handle saws, pole saws, blowers, and hedge trimmers in the same Husqvarna 36V family.
Most crews keep two or three packs rotating through a charger in the truck so a saw is never sitting idle.

body.h: Getting the most life from it
p: Lithium packs last longest when they are not cooked or frozen. Keep them out of direct sun on the dash, let a hot pack cool before charging, and store them partly charged over the off-season. Use a Husqvarna charger and follow Husqvarna's instructions.
Do not use a pack with a cracked case or one that has been crushed or soaked. Retire and recycle damaged batteries. More options are in battery-powered equipment.

faq.q: What tools does the BLi200X fit?
faq.a: It fits Husqvarna 36V battery tools, including pro saws such as the T540iXP and 540iXP, blowers, and trimmers.

faq.q: BLi200X or BLi300?
faq.a: The BLi200X is lighter and suits top-handle work aloft. The BLi300 holds more energy for long ground runs or blowers.

name: Husqvarna BLi300 Li-ion Battery
title: Husqvarna BLi300 Li-ion Battery: Specs and Uses
meta: The Husqvarna BLi300 is a high-capacity 36V Li-ion battery for long runs on Husqvarna saws, blowers, and trimmers. Specs, uses, and care tips inside.
tagline: A large-capacity 36V pack for long ground runs on Husqvarna tools.
summary: The Husqvarna BLi300 is a high-capacity 36V lithium-ion battery for Husqvarna's battery chainsaws, blowers, and trimmers. It carries more energy than the smaller packs, so it suits long ground runs where weight on the tool matters less.
highlights: Long runtime for ground saws and blowers
Good backup pack for the truck

body.h: When the bigger pack makes sense
p: A blower or a rear-handle battery saw on cleanup can drain a small pack fast. The BLi300 roughly doubles the runtime of the mid-size packs, which means fewer swaps on a long day of limbing brush and blowing off driveways. It is heavier, so many climbers keep smaller packs for top-handle saws aloft and run the BLi300 on the ground.
It works across Husqvarna's 36V line, so one pack can move between a saw, pole saw, hedge trimmer, and handheld blower.
Charge with a Husqvarna charger, let hot packs cool first, and keep them out of a closed truck cab in summer heat. For winter storage, leave the pack partly charged in a cool, dry spot.
Retire any battery that has been dropped hard, cracked, or soaked, and recycle it properly. Follow Husqvarna's instructions for use and storage. See more in battery-powered equipment.

faq.q: Will the BLi300 fit a top-handle saw?
faq.a: It fits the Husqvarna 36V platform, but it is heavier than smaller packs, so most climbers choose a lighter battery for work aloft.

faq.q: How long does it take to charge?
faq.a: Charge time depends on the charger model. A Husqvarna rapid charger is much faster than the standard one.

name: Husqvarna 525BX Professional Handheld Blower
title: Husqvarna 525BX Handheld Blower: Specs and Uses
meta: The Husqvarna 525BX is a professional gas handheld blower for clearing sawdust, chips, and leaves after tree work. Specs, uses, and maintenance notes.
tagline: A pro-grade gas handheld blower for fast jobsite cleanup.
summary: The Husqvarna 525BX is a professional gas handheld blower sized for quick cleanup: sawdust off a driveway, chips out of a flower bed, and leaves off a walkway before the crew leaves. It is light enough to grab off the truck for a few minutes of work.
highlights: Fast cleanup of sawdust and chips
Easy to stow on the truck

p: Every tree job leaves sawdust on concrete, chips in the grass, and leaves on the roof edge. A handheld blower clears that faster than a broom. The 525BX is built for professional use, with a two-stroke engine that runs on standard mixed fuel and a compact body that hangs on a truck hook.
For big leaf jobs a backpack blower is still faster, but for finishing a tree job, the handheld is the one you will use daily.

Use fresh, correctly mixed fuel, clean the air filter often in dusty conditions, and check the spark plug at the start of each season. Wear eye and hearing protection, and blow debris away from people, cars, and open windows.
Keep the intake clear of leaves and never point the tube at anyone. Follow Husqvarna's operator manual. More gear is in blowers and other equipment.

faq.q: What fuel does the 525BX use?
faq.a: It is a two-stroke engine that runs on gasoline mixed with two-stroke oil at the ratio in Husqvarna's manual.

faq.q: Handheld or backpack blower for tree work?
faq.a: A handheld is quicker to grab for finishing cleanup. A backpack blower is better for large areas and long leaf jobs.

name: Husqvarna 390XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 390XP Chainsaw: Specs and Buying Guide
meta: The Husqvarna 390XP is an 88 cc professional chainsaw for big felling and bucking work. Engine specs, bar sizes, and how it fits a tree crew's lineup.
tagline: An 88 cc big-wood saw for felling and bucking large trees.
summary: The Husqvarna 390XP is an 88 cc professional chainsaw built for felling and bucking large hardwoods and long bars. It is the saw tree crews pull out when a removal comes down to wood too big for a mid-size saw.
highlights: Runs long bars for large-diameter wood
Built for felling and heavy bucking
Common choice for big removals and storm work

p: Most tree work happens with a mid-size saw. The 390XP is for everything else: big trunks on removals, storm-damaged hardwoods, and stumps that need cutting low. The 88 cc engine pulls a long bar and full-chisel chain through dense wood without bogging, so you finish big cuts with less time in the danger zone.
It is heavy, which is the trade for that power. Pair it with a lighter saw for limbing so you are not swinging a big saw all day.

Match bar and chain to the saw and to the wood, keep the chain sharp, and check chain tension as the bar heats up. Clean the air filter often and keep the cooling fins clear. Big saws throw big kickback, so use correct grip and stance and plan your felling cuts and escape route.
Wear chaps, boots, helmet, eye, and hearing protection, and get trained before running a large saw. More saws are in chainsaws.

faq.q: What bar length suits the 390XP?
faq.a: It is built to run long bars for large wood. Check Husqvarna's recommended bar range for the model and match the chain to the bar.

faq.q: Is the 390XP too much saw for tree service?
faq.a: For daily work most crews use a mid-size saw. The 390XP is the big-wood saw for removals and large storm cleanups.

name: Husqvarna MadSaw Gas-Powered Dielectric Pole Saw
title: Husqvarna MadSaw Gas Dielectric Pole Saw
h1: Husqvarna MadSaw Gas-Powered Dielectric Pole Saw
meta: The Husqvarna MadSaw is a gas-powered dielectric pole saw for reaching limbs from the ground or a bucket. How it is used, and the line clearance cautions.
tagline: A gas pole saw on a dielectric shaft for long-reach limb removal.
summary: The Husqvarna MadSaw is a gas-powered dielectric pole saw that puts a cutting head on an insulated fiberglass shaft for reaching limbs from the ground or a bucket. It is aimed at crews doing high pruning and clearance work who need reach without carrying a saw up the tree.
highlights: Long reach from ground or bucket
No cord or battery to manage
For trained clearance and pruning crews

p: A pole saw lets you take deadwood, clear limbs over roofs and roads, and reduce branch ends without tying in. A gas-powered head on a long dielectric shaft gives you real cutting power at reach, and the fiberglass shaft adds insulation compared with a metal pole. It is a common tool for right-of-way and clearance work from the ground or an aerial lift.
Plan cuts so limbs fall clear of you, the shaft, and anything below. Long cuts at reach are tiring, so take smaller pieces and let gravity work.

A dielectric shaft is not a license to work near power lines. Only qualified line-clearance arborists may work within the minimum approach distances set by OSHA and ANSI Z133, and a dielectric tool must be kept clean, dry, and tested on schedule to keep its rating. Dirt, sap, and moisture on the shaft can conduct.
Wear a helmet, eye and hearing protection, and gloves, and follow Husqvarna's manual and your employer's procedures. More saws are in chainsaws.

faq.q: Does a dielectric pole saw make line work safe?
faq.a: No. It reduces risk only when clean, dry, tested, and used by qualified line-clearance workers who keep the required approach distances.

faq.q: Gas or battery pole saw?
faq.a: Gas gives long runtime and power far from a charger. Battery is quieter and lighter for occasional use.

name: 3/8 in 7-Tooth Clutch Drum for Husqvarna 562XP
title: 3/8 7-Tooth Clutch Drum for Husqvarna 562XP
meta: A replacement 3/8 in 7-tooth clutch drum for the Husqvarna 562XP chainsaw. When to replace it, how to check wear, and matching it to your chain pitch.
tagline: A replacement 3/8 in pitch, 7-tooth clutch drum for the 562XP.
summary: This replacement Husqvarna 562XP clutch drum is set up for 3/8 in pitch chain with a 7-tooth drive. Swap it in when the drum is worn or when you change the saw over to 3/8 in chain for bigger bars and wood.
highlights: Replaces a worn or grooved drum
Matches 3/8 in chain and bar setups
Inspect the needle bearing at the same time

body.h: When to replace the clutch drum
p: The drum takes the clutch's full load and the chain's wear. Look for deep grooves worn into the drive teeth or rim, a bluish heat-discolored inner surface from a slipping clutch, or a drum that wobbles on the shaft. A worn drum chews through new chains, so change it on the same schedule as a couple of chain replacements.
Pitch has to match across the chain, bar, and drive. If you are switching the 562XP from .325 to 3/8 in chain, you need a 3/8 in drum and a bar with a matching nose sprocket.

Remove the clutch cover, bar, and chain, then take off the clutch to reach the drum. Check the needle bearing and grease it or replace it if it feels rough. Reinstall the clutch per the manual, note that it usually loosens clockwise, and fit a chain of matching pitch.

Shut the engine off, let it cool, and remove the spark plug boot or battery before working on the saw. Follow the Husqvarna workshop or operator manual for torque and reassembly, and test-run the saw before it goes back in service. Find more in chainsaw parts.

faq.q: Can I run 3/8 in chain on a 562XP?
faq.a: Yes, with a 3/8 in drive drum, a matching bar, and 3/8 in chain. All three must match.

faq.q: How often should the drum be replaced?
faq.a: Replace it when the drive teeth or rim show deep wear grooves, typically after a few chains.

name: .325 7-Tooth Rim Sprocket
title: .325 7-Tooth Rim Sprocket for Chainsaws
meta: A replacement .325 rim sprocket with 7 teeth for chainsaws that run .325 pitch chain. How to check wear, match the spline, and when to swap it out.
tagline: A .325 pitch, 7-tooth replacement rim sprocket for mid-size saws.
summary: This .325 rim sprocket has 7 teeth and replaces the floating drive ring on saws that run .325 pitch chain. Rim sprockets are cheap, quick to swap, and the easiest way to keep a fresh chain from wearing out early.
highlights: Easy swap without replacing the drum
Confirm spline type for your saw

p: A rim sprocket is a loose ring that slides onto a splined clutch drum. It floats slightly so it lines up with the bar and chain, and when it wears you replace just the ring, not the whole drum. Worn rims show grooves where the drive links ride. Running a new chain on a grooved rim wears the chain fast and can make it jump.
Common practice is to replace the rim every second or third chain. A 7-tooth .325 rim is a standard size on many mid-size saws.

Rim sprockets come with different spline counts, so match the spline pattern on your saw's drum, as well as pitch and tooth count. Remove the bar, chain, and E-clip or washer, slide the old rim off, check the drum for wear, and fit the new rim.
Shut the saw off and let it cool before working on it, and follow the manufacturer's manual. More parts are in chainsaw parts.

faq.q: How do I know my spline count?
faq.a: Count the splines on your clutch drum or check the saw's parts list. The rim must match the drum's spline pattern.

faq.q: Rim or spur sprocket?
faq.a: A rim is a replaceable ring on a splined drum. A spur sprocket is fixed to the drum, so the whole drum is replaced.

name: .325 7-Tooth Spur Sprocket
title: .325 7-Tooth Spur Sprocket for Chainsaws
meta: A .325 spur sprocket with 7 teeth for chainsaws running .325 pitch chain. Learn when to replace it, how it differs from a rim sprocket, and fitment.
tagline: A .325 pitch, 7-tooth spur-style drive sprocket for chainsaws.
summary: This .325 spur sprocket has 7 teeth and drives .325 pitch chain on saws built around a fixed spur drive. Replace it when the teeth are hooked or worn, and you will get full life out of new chains.
highlights: Protects new chains from early wear
Confirm fit with your saw model

body.h: Spur drives and when to swap them
p: On a spur drive, the sprocket teeth are fixed to the clutch drum. There is no floating ring to replace, so when the teeth wear, the whole spur sprocket gets changed. Look for teeth that have gone pointed or hooked, or a groove where the drive links ride. A worn spur sprocket wears chain quickly and can cause the chain to jump under load.
Some saws come with a spur drive from the factory, and some owners prefer them for simplicity. A rim setup is cheaper to maintain over time, but a spur is perfectly serviceable.

faq.q: Does tooth count matter?

name: Anti-Vibration Element for Husqvarna 372XP
title: Anti-Vibration Element for Husqvarna 372XP
meta: A replacement anti vibration element for the Husqvarna 372XP chainsaw. Signs of worn AV mounts, why they matter for your hands, and replacement tips.
tagline: A replacement AV element that restores the 372XP's vibration damping.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP anti vibration element replaces a worn, cracked, or stretched AV mount on the saw. Fresh mounts cut the buzz reaching your hands and keep the handle and engine aligned.
highlights: Replace worn mounts as a set

p: Husqvarna pro saws separate the handles from the engine with anti-vibration elements. Every hour of cutting flexes those mounts, and over time they sag, crack, or break. Signs include more buzz in the handles, a handle that moves or clunks against the body, or a chain brake handle that rubs. Running on failed mounts means more vibration in your hands and more strain on the saw.

The 372XP is a long-serving pro saw, and many in service have thousands of hours on the original mounts. If your 372XP feels harsher than it used to, the AV elements are one of the first things to check.

Note where each mount sits before you remove anything, because positions can differ. Many crews replace all the mounts at once so the saw feels even. Check that the handle sits square and moves only as much as designed after the job.
Shut the saw off, let it cool, and follow Husqvarna's workshop manual. Find more in chainsaw parts.

faq.q: How do I know the AV mounts are bad?
faq.a: More vibration in the handles, a loose or clunking handle, or a visible crack or stretched spring are common signs.

faq.q: Should I replace all AV elements at once?
faq.a: It is common practice. Mixing old and new mounts can leave the saw unbalanced in your hands.

name: Carburetor Assembly for Husqvarna T540XP Mark II
title: Carburetor Assembly for Husqvarna T540XP Mark II
h1: Carburetor Assembly for Husqvarna T540XP Mark II
meta: A replacement T540XP Mark II carburetor assembly for Husqvarna's pro top-handle saw. Symptoms of a failing carb, what to check first, and install notes.
tagline: A replacement carburetor assembly for the T540XP Mark II top-handle saw.
summary: This T540XP Mark II carburetor assembly is a replacement for the carb on Husqvarna's professional top-handle saw. It is the fix when a saw will not idle, hesitates, or runs poorly and the cheaper causes have been ruled out.
highlights: Works with the saw's AutoTune system
Rule out fuel and air issues first

p: Most running problems on a top-handle saw are not the carburetor. Before replacing it, check for stale or wrongly mixed fuel, a clogged fuel filter, a dirty air filter, a fouled spark plug, a blocked spark arrestor screen, and cracked fuel lines. Old ethanol fuel left in a saw over the off-season is a common cause of varnished carbs.

If the saw still will not hold an idle, bogs, or floods after those checks, a new carburetor assembly is often faster and more reliable than rebuilding a varnished one, especially on a climbing saw you depend on.

The T540XP Mark II uses AutoTune, so follow Husqvarna's procedure for fitting the carb and letting the system relearn; a dealer can also check it with Husqvarna's service tools. Reconnect the fuel line and throttle linkage carefully, and confirm the chain does not turn at idle before using the saw.
Shut the saw off and let it cool before servicing. A saw that runs badly aloft is a safety problem, so test it on the ground first. More parts are in chainsaw parts.

faq.q: Does the T540XP Mark II carburetor need adjusting?
faq.a: The saw uses AutoTune, which adjusts the mixture automatically. Follow Husqvarna's instructions after installing a new carb.

faq.q: What causes carburetor problems?
faq.a: Stale or ethanol-heavy fuel, dirt past the filters, and long storage with fuel in the saw are the usual causes.
